plan, notes, research, sim\n```\n\n**Missing from implementation (from original plan):**\n- `core/fountain/degree.ts` — degree distribution logic (D6, D25)\n- `core/block/bitmap.ts` — block bitmap for D22 resume\n- `core/block/schedule.ts` — dwell scheduling (§8.1) and repair code (§8.2)\n- `core/frame/repair-code.ts` — repair code format (§7.6, §8.2)\n- `core/hash/stream-id.ts` — streamId derivation (§7.5)\n- `modulation/qr-tiled/layout.ts` — tile layout logic\n- `modulation/qr-tiled/ladder.ts` — D16 ladder rung logic\n- `workers/opfs.worker.ts` — OPFS worker (may be inline elsewhere)\n\n**Module-to-phase map.** Each unwritten core module is assigned to a specific phase based on when its functionality is first required by exit criteria or invariants. This map prevents \"module exists but has no owner\" gaps.\n\n| Module | Phase | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| `core/frame/beacon.ts` | **1** | Beacon packet encoding/decoding (§7.2, D17/D21) is framing — Phase 1's \"framing\" deliverable. Required for the receiver to learn file metadata (`streamId`, `blockCount`, `K`, etc.) before it can interpret any payload packet. |\n| `core/hash/stream-id.ts` | **1** | `streamId` derivation (§7.4, D7) is required by the fountain encoder's PRNG seeding. Phase 1's \"LT encode\" and \"GE decode\" cannot work without `streamId`, and I3's conformance vector depends on it. |\n| `core/hash/block-hash.ts` | **1** | Per-block hashes (§7.3) are the only application-layer integrity check on payload bytes (§7.1). Phase 1's \"byte-exact\" requirement (property tests) and I9's verification invariant cannot be enforced without them. |\n| `core/block/schedule.ts` | **4** | Dwell scheduling (§8.1) and repair code targeting (§8.2) are large-file machinery. Phase 4's A5 (synthetic 4 GB), A6 (resume), and A7 (repair) exit criteria require block scheduling. |\n| `core/frame/repair-code.ts` | **4** | Repair code format (§7.6, §8.2) is the human-mediated recovery path. Phase 4's A7 exit criterion (\"Only the missing blocks retransmit\") requires encoding/decoding repair codes. |\n\n**Rules.** `core/` MUST NOT import from `modulation/`, `workers/`, `platform/` or `ui/` —\nit is the layer the property tests own. Nothing outside `modulation/` may reference QR\n(§6.1 modulation is swappable). Every browser capability check lives in\n`platform/capabilities.ts`, never inline at a call site, so §16.1's platform matrix has\nexactly one implementation.\n\n**Dependency contract.** Exact-pinned, no ranges, no post-install scripts (gate G3).\n\n| Dependency | Pin | If unavailable |\n|---|---|---|\n| `zxing-wasm` | exact version + SRI on the `.wasm`. **MUST call `setZXingModuleOverrides({ locateFile })` pointing at a bundle-local, service-worker-precached `.wasm`.** See the general WASM rule below | Fatal on the receiver — surface `E-WASM-LOAD`; the sender still works |\n| `incremental-wasm-hash` | exact version + SRI on the `.wasm`. **MUST be bundle-local, service-worker-precached, and loaded via bundle-local overrides (not default CDN paths).** See the general WASM rule below | Fatal on the receiver — surface `E-WASM-LOAD`; per-block hashes alone are insufficient for byte-exact reconstruction per concept.md constraint 4 |\n| `node-qrcode` | exact version | Fatal on the sender; the receiver still works |\n| `CompressionStream` | platform | Skip compression (D8 is already conditional) |\n| `MediaStreamTrackProcessor` | platform | Fall back to `requestVideoFrameCallback` + `drawImage` — MUST be implemented, it is not Chromium-only |\n| OPFS | platform | Refuse large files; cap at in-memory size and say so |\n| Wake Lock | platform | Warn before a long transfer (`E-WAKELOCK-LOST`) |\n\n> ### ⚠️ EVERY WASM dependency MUST be bundle-local and SRI-pinned\n>\n> **This is a general rule, not specific to zxing.** Any package that loads WASM from a\n> CDN by default voids the entire premise. The receiver:\n>\n> 1. makes a **third-party network request mid-session** — voiding T7, concept.md\n>    constraint 1, and the README's \"provably no exfiltration\";\n> 2. **fails completely in airplane mode** — i.e. in the flagship air-gapped use case (A8);\n> 3. **executes remotely-fetched WASM** — precisely the supply-chain surface T5 exists for.\n>\n> **Every WASM dependency MUST:**\n>\n> - Be bundled with the application (not fetched from a CDN)\n> - Have its `.wasm` file SRI-pinned in the lockfile (integrity hash)\n> - Be precached by the service worker for offline operation\n> - Be loaded via bundle-local overrides, not default CDN paths\n>\n> **Current WASM dependencies covered by this rule:**\n>\n> - `zxing-wasm`: MUST call `setZXingModuleOverrides({ locateFile })` pointing at a\n>   bundle-local, service-worker-precached `.wasm`\n> - `incremental-wasm-hash` (the whole-file hasher): MUST be bundle-local and\n>   service-worker-precached; used for the mandatory whole-file hash (§7.2)\n>\n> §14.4's no-network assertion covers this — it MUST exercise every WASM code path to\n> detect CDN fetches. For zxing, this means the assertion must perform a decode; for the\n> hasher, it must hash a non-empty stream.\n\n**Cross-origin isolation.** The pipeline uses transferable `VideoFrame`s and\n`ArrayBuffer`s, **not** `SharedArrayBuffer` — so COOP/COEP headers are **not** required.\nThis is deliberate: requiring them would constrain static hosting for no gain. Any future\nuse of `SharedArrayBuffer` is a hosting decision, not just a code change.\n\n### 6.6 The luma-vs-colour disagreement, and how it is resolved\n\n| | `custom-codec-engineering.md` §7.2 | `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` §6.6 |\n|---|---|---|\n| Colour cell penalty under 4:2:0 | 2× linear (4× area) — **derived** | 1.25× linear (1.56× area) — **measured** |\n| Verdict | luma-only wins ~1.95× | RGB-tripling wins **1.98×** |\n\nThe measured result is better founded and the mechanism convincing: **chroma decimation\nis a low-pass filter, not a deletion.** A binary chroma pattern at 5 px/module presents\n2.5 chroma samples per module — above Nyquist; at 4 px/module exactly 2.0, right at\nNyquist, which is where the measurement breaks. The \"2× per axis\" rule over-corrects by\nrestoring the *original* sampling density rather than staying above Nyquist in the\ndecimated grid.\n\nAlso weighing against luma-only: 8-level luma measured **unusable** under handheld blur\n(21.2% symbol error at 5 px/cell) vs **0.00%** for saturated 8-colour at 4 px/cell; and\n**libcimbar spends 2 of its 6 bits per cell on colour**, with its deprecated 8-colour\nmode benchmarking *faster*.\n\n**Resolution (D11): neither document decides.** A calibration probe measures the device\nat session start. Where the luma-side note is unambiguously right: **AWB warps colour in\nthree non-monotonic dimensions** and cannot be locked on iOS, so a per-frame in-band\ncolour reference is **not optional** for Stage 2.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Data model\n\n### 7.1 Payload packet header — 13 bytes\n\n| Offset | Size | Field | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | 1 | `magic_ver` | 4-bit magic + 4-bit wire version. Rejects foreign QR instantly. See §16.3 for version skew. |\n| 1 | 1 | `flags` | packet type (payload/beacon), reserved |\n| 2 | 4 | `streamId` | Identifies the **file**. Seeds the PRNG; receiver locks it on first sight. Derivation: §7.5 |\n| 6 | 3 | `blockIndex` | 16.7 M blocks × 192 KB = **3.0 TB** addressable — beyond any practical transfer (1 TB is 117 days) |\n| 9 | 3 | `seq` | Sequence **within the block**; with `streamId`+`blockIndex` derives the index set |\n| 12 | 1 | `fcrc` | CRC-8 — rejects a mis-decode before it poisons the matrix |\n\n`K`, `L` and the index set remain **derived, never transmitted** (I3).\n\n**`fcrc` covers bytes 0–11 only — the header, NOT the payload.** This is deliberate: CRC-8\nover 269 bytes would be weak anyway, and the header is what must be trusted before a packet\nis routed to a block. But the consequence must be stated plainly:\n\n> **A packet whose header is intact and whose 256-byte payload is corrupted passes `fcrc`\n> unconditionally and poisons the GE matrix.** `fcrc` is a routing guard, not an integrity\n> check.\n\nPayload integrity therefore rests on exactly two things: QR's own Reed–Solomon (which makes\nan undetected symbol error rare, but not impossible) and **the per-block hash (§7.3), which\nis the sole application-layer check on payload bytes.** The manifest-based hash verification\nensures corrupted blocks are detected before completion: a block that reaches rank K but fails\nits hash is never surfaced to the user and triggers re-collection (`E-BLOCK-HASH`, §11, E12).\nI9 enforces that unverified blocks written to OPFS are never exported or made visible to\nthe user until the manifest arrives and verification succeeds. A test MUST corrupt a payload\nbyte and assert the block hash catches it — corrupting only header bytes, as the current\nsuite does, cannot detect this class at all.\n\n### 7.2 Beacon packet (D17/D21)\n\nEmitted every ~2 s at the most conservative profile. Everything the receiver needs before\nit can interpret any payload packet:\n\n| Field | Size | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `streamId` | 4 | Must match payload packets |\n| `wireVersion` | 1 | Full version, not the 4-bit nibble |\n| `originalSize` | 6 | Original uncompressed file size — 281 TB addressable, **MUST be bounds-checked** (§12, T1) |\n| `payloadLen` | 6 | Actual payload length after compression (if enabled); required to compute the last block's short length — `blockCount * blockSize` is an upper bound only |\n| `blockSize`, `blockCount` | 3 + 3 | Yields K (blockSize / L). Last block short length is derived from `payloadLen`, not from blockSize alone. |\n| `fragmentLen` (L) | 2 | Fixed for the session (I1) |\n| `degreeCap` | 1 | D25; receiver MUST use the same cap |\n| `flags` | 1 | compressed / hash alg / colour profile |\n| `blockHashLen` | 1 | Per-block hash truncation length |\n| `wholeFileHash` | 32 | **Mandatory.** concept.md constraint 4 makes byte-exact reconstruction non-negotiable and names this as the verification. An earlier revision made it optional \"on very large files\" — i.e. dropped the guarantee exactly where E5 (source mutated during a 10-hour read) is most likely and the stakes are highest. Computed on the **decompressed reassembly** (after decompression, if compression is enabled; otherwise on the received blocks directly). The sender hashes the original file by streaming it through an incremental WASM hasher; the receiver hashes its decompressed output and compares. The hash covers the final user-visible output, not intermediate compressed data. If decompression fails (E15), the hash cannot be evaluated and the compressed artefact is kept unverified. |\n| `manifestHash` | 4 | **Mandatory.** CRC-32 of the manifest data (§7.3). Roots the cryptographic chain: **beacon → manifest → blocks → whole file**. Without this, a corrupted manifest packet would cause wrong block hashes, leading to infinite E12 failures with no error code or termination. The beacon already carries 32 bytes; adding 4 more is negligible. |\n| `filenameLen` | 1 | Length prefix for filename field |\n| `filename` | var | UTF-8 filename, **sanitised** (§12, T2). Capped at 128 bytes / 32 codepoints. See truncation rules below. |\n| `mimeTypeLen` | 1 | Length prefix for MIME type field |\n| `mimeType` | var | UTF-8 MIME type. Capped at 58 bytes / 14 codepoints. |\n| `beaconCRC` | 4 | **Mandatory.** CRC-32 covering all beacon fields above. Validated before any beacon metadata is trusted. |\n\n**Beacon size bound calculation (R1's 256-byte payload):**\n- Fixed fields: 64 bytes (streamId, wireVersion, originalSize, payloadLen, blockSize, blockCount, fragmentLen, degreeCap, flags, blockHashLen, wholeFileHash, manifestHash)\n- CRC-32: 4 bytes (beacon integrity)\n- Length prefixes: 2 bytes (filenameLen, mimeTypeLen)\n- **Available for filename + mimeType: 256 − 64 − 4 − 2 = 186 bytes**\n\n**Allocation:**\n- Filename: 128 bytes max, 32 UTF-8 codepoints max\n- MIME type: 58 bytes max, 14 UTF-8 codepoints max\n- Total: 186 bytes (exactly fits available space)\n\n**Filename truncation strategy (T2):**\n1. **Strip path separators, control bytes, and leading dots** — prevents directory traversal and filesystem attacks\n2. **Truncate to 32 UTF-8 codepoints max** — conservative bound ensuring we never exceed 128 bytes (worst case: 32 × 4 = 128)\n3. **Preserve file extension when possible** — if truncating, keep \".ext\" suffix for usability\n4. **Validate UTF-8 byte length** — ensure final encoded string fits in 128-byte beacon budget\n5. **Fallback to \"received-file\"** — if filename is empty after sanitization\n\nThis strategy ensures the beacon never overflows R1's 256-byte payload while accommodating common filenames and MIME types. A 255-byte UTF-8 filename (legal on most filesystems) is safely truncated with no ambiguity.\n\nThe receiver shows \"acquiring…\" until its first beacon.\n\n### 7.3 The block-hash manifest — how per-block hashes reach the receiver\n\nI9, E12, §6.4, §8.3 and §7.4 all depend on per-block hashes, and §7.1 establishes they are\nthe *only* application-layer check on payload bytes. Nothing in the wire format carried\nthem: the 13-byte header has no room, and the beacon carries only `blockHashLen`.\n\n**A 4 GB file has 21,845 blocks. Even 4-byte hashes are 87 KB — far beyond a beacon.**\n\n**Resolution: hashes travel as a manifest, fountain-coded like any other block.**\n\n| Property | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Transport | A dedicated **manifest stream**, `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF`, distinguished by `PacketFlags.Manifest` |\n| Contents | `blockCount × blockHashLen` truncated hashes, in block order |\n| Integrity | **Mandatory validation via beacon's `manifestHash` field (§7.2)**. The beacon carries a 4-byte CRC-32 of the manifest data. After decoding the manifest, the receiver MUST compute its CRC-32 and compare against the beacon's `manifestHash`. A mismatch indicates corruption and MUST cause the manifest to be discarded and re-decoded. This prevents infinite E12 failures from corrupted manifest data. |\n| `blockHashLen` | **4 bytes.** Per-block false accept 2⁻³², ~5×10⁻⁶ across 21,845 blocks — comfortably below the whole-file hash's job |\n| Coding | **Fixed K=768 multi-block stream** — `blockCount_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)`, same LT encoder, same GE decoder. Each manifest block is fountain-coded independently, inheriting the flat-cost property. |\n| Cadence | Interleaved with payload on the same schedule as the beacon (D17), so a late joiner acquires it without waiting a pass |\n| Before it arrives | Completed blocks are written to OPFS but tracked separately from verified blocks (two-bitmap system: `complete` for decoded, `writtenBlocks` for written). They are verified retroactively once the manifest decodes. The receiver reports \"verifying…\" rather than claiming completion. **Critical: blocks written before verification are NEVER surfaced to the user or exported until their hash is verified (I9).** |\n\n**Why not append the hash to each block's payload:** it would make the payload\n`blockSize + 4`, breaking `blockSize = K·L` and therefore D19's entire arithmetic and G7.\n\n**Sizing sanity:** 21,845 blocks × 4 B = 87 KB at 4 GB ⇒ `blockCount_manifest` = 1 (one block). At 100 GB (546,125 blocks): 2.1 MB ⇒ 11 blocks. At 1 TB (5.46M blocks): 21 MB ⇒ 110 blocks. Each block decodes at K=768 (72 KB matrix), so memory stays bounded regardless of file size — flat-cost by design.\n\n> **G7 gate targets:** For a **4 GB file**, **21,845 blocks** produce an **87 KB manifest** (one 192 KB block).\n\n**Why the manifest hash is mandatory:** Without it, a single flipped byte in the manifest\npacket would yield wrong hashes for hundreds of blocks. Those blocks would fail E12 forever\n— re-collect, fail, re-collect — with no error code and no termination. The manifest hash\ndetects this corruption immediately and forces re-decode of the manifest.\n\n### 7.4 Session state\n\n```ts\ntype SendSession = {\n  source: File;\n  staging: FileSystemFileHandle | null;   // compressed copy (D8) — MUST be wiped\n  streamId: number;\n  blockSize: number; blockCount: number;\n  readonly fragmentLen: number;           // L — I1\n  readonly K: number;                     // D26\n  cursor: { blockIndex: number; seq: number };\n  dwellPackets: number;                   // §8.1\n};\n\ntype RecvSession = {\n  streamId: number | null;                // locked on first valid header\n  meta: BeaconMeta | null;                // gates everything\n  complete: Uint8Array;                   // block bitmap — tracks decoded blocks\n  writtenBlocks: Uint8Array;              // bitmap tracking blocks written to OPFS\n  active: { blockIndex: number; pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5 — payload block GE context\n  manifestActive: { pivots: Map<number, GERow>; rank: number } | null;  // I5 — manifest block GE context\n  manifest: BlockHashManifest | null;    // §7.3 — persisted for resume\n  out: PositionalWriteHandle | null;      // OPFS positional write (worker-only createSyncAccessHandle)\n  stats: { fps: number; cameraPxPerModule: number; packetsPerSec: number; eta: number };\n};\n```\n\n**Two-bitmap system:** `complete` tracks blocks that have been fountain-decoded; `writtenBlocks` tracks blocks that have been written to OPFS. These separate because blocks may be decoded before their hashes arrive (§7.3), and they must not be surfaced to the user until verified.\n\nPartial state for a block the sender has moved past is **discarded, not persisted** — a\nbadly damaged block rarely half-completes usefully, and persisting it would defeat I6.\nThe bitmap is tiny: 4 GB / 192 KB = 21,845 blocks = **2.7 KB**.\n\n### 7.5 `streamId` derivation\n\nLoad-bearing: D22 resume requires that re-selecting the same file reproduces the same\n`streamId`. The derivation uses sampling to avoid the cost of hashing the full file payload.\n\n**Derivation (sender):**\n\n```\nstreamId = CRC32( originalSize ‖ first 64 KB ‖ middle 64 KB ‖ last 64 KB ‖ lastModified )\n```\n\n**Critical:** `originalSize` is the **uncompressed** file size (the beacon's `originalSize` field), NOT the compressed payload size (`payloadLen`). This is required because:\n\n- **Resume (D22):** `streamId` identifies the FILE the user selected, not the compressed version. Using `originalSize` ensures the same file always produces the same `streamId` regardless of compression settings.\n- **Security separation:** E3a's block arithmetic uses `payloadLen` (compressed size) from the beacon to compute the last block's short length. T1's quota check, T3's decompression-bomb cap, and D23's ETA all use `originalSize` from the beacon. `streamId` participates in the original-size domain because it identifies the user's chosen file.\n\nThree sampled windows plus size and mtime. Costs ~200 KB of reads regardless of file\nsize, so it is instant even for 4 TB.\n\n**What this buys and what it does not:**\n\n- ✅ Same file re-selected → same `streamId` → resume works.\n- ✅ Different files → different `streamId` with overwhelming probability.\n- ⚠️ A file edited **only in the middle**, keeping size and mtime, collides. Mitigated by\n  including `lastModified`, and by per-block hashes catching the mismatch at block level.\n- ⚠️ This is **not** a content-integrity hash. The whole-file hash (§7.2) **is** a\n  content-integrity hash and is mandatory per concept.md constraint 4. `streamId` is an *identifier*.\n\nDeliberately **not** `crc32(payload)` — the research's original design — because the\nblock layer made a full-payload pass unaffordable.\n\n### 7.6 Repair code format (§8.2)\n\nA human types this, so it must be short, unambiguous, and self-checking.\n\n```\nSF1-<streamId32>-<ranges32>-<check>\n```\n\n- **Alphabet:** Crockford base32 (no I/L/O/U — removes the common misreadings).\n- **`ranges`:** run-length encoded missing-block set. Contiguous runs are the common case\n  because misses cluster (the user looked away).\n- **`check`:** 2 characters, CRC-8 over the decoded body. A mistyped code MUST be\n  rejected, never acted on — acting on a corrupted range wastes hours.\n- **Length bound:** if the encoded form exceeds **48 characters**, the receiver MUST\n  instead offer a QR containing the same payload (which the sender's camera reads, or the\n  user photographs), and say so. A 100 GB file with scattered misses can exceed any\n  reasonable typing length, and silently truncating the set would be a correctness bug.\n\n### 7.7 Normative wire constants\n\nThe following constants are **fixed in code** and **MUST** be reproduced exactly by any\nthird-party implementation. They are not subject to negotiation or configuration; changing\nany of these is a wire-format breaking change (§16.3). These are what §14.3's conformance\nvectors exist to validate.\n\n| Constant | Value | Purpose | Location |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **MAGIC** | `0x5` | 4-bit magic in header `magic_ver` field; used for fast rejection of foreign QR symbols. The high nibble of byte 0 in every packet header. | `src/core/params.ts` |\n| **WIRE_VERSION** | `1` | 4-bit wire version in header `magic_ver` field; indicates wire format revision. Packets with mismatched versions are rejected with `E-VERSION`. | `src/core/params.ts` |\n| **L (fragment length)** | `256` | Fixed fragment length in bytes for wire version 1. **NOT session-negotiable** — part of the wire format. The beacon transmits fragmentLen as a validity check; receivers MUST reject any beacon where fragmentLen ≠ L with `E-VERSION`. L cannot change without incrementing WIRE_VERSION. | `src/core/params.ts` |\n| **CRC-8 polynomial** | `0x31` | CRC-8 polynomial used for `fcrc` field in packet headers (covers bytes 0–11 only). | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n| **CRC-8 initial value** | `0xff` | Initial CRC value for CRC-8 computation. | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n| **CRC-32 polynomial** | `0xedb88320` | IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 polynomial used for `streamId` derivation (§7.4), `manifestHash` (§7.2), and `beaconCRC` (§7.2). This is the standard IEEE polynomial (reversed representation). | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n| **CRC-32 initial value** | `0xffffffff` | Initial CRC value for CRC-32 computation (XORed with seed, final XOR with `0xffffffff`). | `src/core/frame/crc.ts` |\n| **SplitMix32 increment** | `0x9e3779b9` | Golden ratio φ = 2³²/φ, used to increment state in SplitMix32 PRNG. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n| **SplitMix32 round 1 multiplier** | `0x21f0aaad` | First mixing constant in SplitMix32 avalanche. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n| **SplitMix32 round 2 multiplier** | `0x735a2d97` | Second mixing constant in SplitMix32 avalanche. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n| **packetSeed round 1 multiplier** | `0x85ebca6b` | First mixing constant when combining `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. **Order is normative** — changing the order of operations or the constants changes the derived index set. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n| **packetSeed round 2 multiplier** | `0xc2b2ae35` | Second mixing constant when combining `(streamId, blockIndex, seq)`. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n| **Partial Fisher-Yates algorithm** | Fisher-Yates shuffle truncated at `d` iterations | Generates `d` distinct indices from `[0, k)` without rejection sampling. Critical for bounded-time index derivation. The algorithm is: (1) initialize `pool[i] = i` for `i in [0, k)`, (2) for `i in [0, d)`: `j = i + floor(rnd() * (k - i))`, swap `pool[i]` and `pool[j]`, return `pool[i]`. **This exact algorithm is normative** — any change produces different index sets. | `src/core/fountain/prng.ts` |\n\n**Implementation notes:**\n\n- All CRC implementations use the standard definitions: CRC-8 uses polynomial `0x31` (ITU-T I.432.1 / ATM HEC) with initial value `0xff`; CRC-32 uses the IEEE 802.3 polynomial with initial/final XOR `0xffffffff`.\n- SplitMix32 is a simple PRNG sufficient for fountain code index selection. The constants shown are the standard ones from the algorithm's definition.\n- `packetSeed` mixes three 32-bit values (streamId, blockIndex, seq) into one 32-bit seed for SplitMix32. The exact mixing order and constants are **normative** — a different implementation must produce identical output for the same inputs, or index sets will not match and fountain decoding will fail.\n- The partial Fisher-Yates shuffle is critical: it produces exactly `d` distinct indices in `[0, k)` with O(d) time and O(k) space. A naïve rejection-sampling approach would have unbounded time and is **forbidden**.\n\n**Conformance testing:** §14.3 requires test vectors covering `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` to validate the entire PRNG chain (packetSeed → SplitMix32 → partial Fisher-Yates). Any implementation change to the constants or algorithms above breaks these vectors and is a wire-format violation.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Behaviour at gigabyte scale\n\n### 8.1 Block scheduling and the dwell budget\n\nThe sender does not know which blocks the receiver has, so it dwells on each block for\n`dwellPackets`, then advances, looping the file continuously.\n\n**Dwell must survive the top of the assumed erasure band.** An earlier revision paired\ndwell 1.4 K with a 20–30% band, which failed at the top of its own band — at 30%\nerasure, 1.4 K delivers 0.98 K against the ~1.02 K needed, so **every block missed its\nfirst pass**, each costing a full extra pass.\n\nThe fix is to raise dwell, **not** to narrow the band. Narrowing it (a briefly-adopted\nmistake) contradicts the evidence base, which specifies 20–30% and warns that driving\nerasure lower means the ladder is too conservative and throughput is being left unused.\n\n| dwell | 20% erasure | 25% | **30%** | needed |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1.4 K | 1.120 K | 1.050 K | **0.980 K ❌** | ~1.02 K |\n| **1.6 K** | 1.280 K | 1.200 K | **1.120 K ✅** | ~1.02 K |\n\n> **G7 gate target:** At the adopted design, **dwell = 1.6 K** (default, tunable).\n\n- **dwell = 1.6 × K** (default; tunable)\n- **assumed band = 20–30%** (D18c) — an assumption, not a controlled target\n\nA test MUST assert `dwell × (1 − erasure_max) ≥ 1.12`, matching §13.1's +12% p99\noverhead budget, so dwell and the band cannot drift apart again.\n\n**The e_max completion cliff.** A block completes on a pass iff `dwell × (1 − e) ≥ 1 + overhead`.\nAt dwell 1.6 K and the measured +4.2% p99 overhead (D25, §13.1):\n```\ne_max = 1 − 1.042 / 1.6 = 34.9%\n```\n\n> **G7 gate target:** At dwell 1.6 K and +4.2% p99 overhead, **e_max = 34.9% completion cliff**. The 30% repair code trigger provides a 4.9% buffer below this cliff.\n\n**Note:** The test requirement uses 1.12 (the +12% budget from §13.1) as a conservative margin. The actual measured p99 overhead is +4.2%, giving the true completion cliff at 34.9% erasure. The 30% repair code trigger (line 864) provides a 4.9% buffer below this cliff.\nAbove this erasure rate, every pass delivers **less than K independent packets** — the block\nnever reaches full rank, the decoder resets, and the next pass starts from rank 0. **The transfer\nNEVER FINISHES**, at any file size, with the progress bar frozen at zero blocks. This is why the\nrepair code (§8.2) exists: when real erasure exceeds e_max, human mediation is the designed recovery path.\n\n**When real erasure exceeds 30%** — which nothing in v1 can detect (D18a) — blocks miss\nand the **repair code (§8.2) is the recovery path**, not a tighter loop. This is the\ndesigned answer, not a gap.\n\n**Dwell is a standing ~60% overhead.** The sender always emits 1.6× what a block needs,\nwhatever the channel. §13.1's throughput budgets are stated **after** this factor —\nthey are goodput, not wire rate.\n\n### 8.2 Human-mediated repair — the cheap back-channel\n\nThe receiver knows exactly which blocks it lacks. The user reads a code off one screen and\ntypes it into the other:\n\n> **Receiver:** \"Missing 3 blocks. Repair code: `SF1-K7F2M9-3B-X4`\"\n> **Sender:** [paste] → transmits only those blocks\n\nTurns a multi-hour extra pass into a sub-minute repair, needs no second camera and no\ngeometry constraints, and is what makes small blocks (§3.4) affordable. Format: §7.6.\n\n### 8.3 Resume (D22)\n\nThe receiver persists `{streamId, meta, complete, writtenBlocks, manifest}` plus the OPFS output after every completed\nblock. On reload it offers to resume. At 2.7 KB per 4 GB for the bitmaps this is nearly free; the manifest adds\n87 KB for a 4 GB file (21,845 blocks × 4-byte hashes). **The manifest MUST be persisted** — without it,\nresume cannot re-verify blocks, and a reload during the ~12 minute manifest acquisition window would lose\nall received blocks.\n\nThe sender is stateless across restarts by construction (D24) **when compression is disabled** —\nit needs only the same file and the same `streamId` (§7.4). **With compression enabled, resume is\nNOT supported** — see `docs/notes/bf-17s0-resume-compression-conflict.md` for the full analysis,\n`docs/notes/bf-3k90-compression-resume-solution-evaluation.md` for the solution evaluation,\nand `notes/bf-2w1a.md` for validation and test coverage.\nThe short version: `CompressionStream` offers no determinism guarantee, so re-compression after\nstaging is reaped (E11) would produce different blocks and silently corrupt the receiver's state.\nThe beacon carries a `ResumeDisabled` flag (beacon `flags` field) when compression is on;\nthe receiver uses this flag to suppress resume UI and prevent persisting resume tokens.\nThis preserves the T4 privacy requirement (staging is still wiped on startup) while preventing\nsilent corruption.\n\n**On resume the receiver MUST re-verify block hashes** rather than trusting the bitmap, in\ncase OPFS was corrupted or the file was touched externally. This requires the manifest to be\npersisted alongside the bitmap.\n\n**Pre-manifest reload behavior:** If the receiver is reloaded before the manifest arrives\n(e.g., during the ~12 minute acquisition window for a 4 GB file at the beacon's ~2 s cadence),\nthe persisted bitmap preserves which blocks were decoded, and the written blocks remain in OPFS.\nThe `writtenBlocks` bitmap is reset on resume, and blocks are re-verified once the manifest arrives.\nThis prevents losing all received blocks during the manifest acquisition window.\n\n### 8.4 Storage limits\n\n| Platform | Practical quota |\n|---|---|\n| Chrome / Edge desktop | ~60% of free disk — multi-GB fine |\n| Firefox | ~10% of disk (capped ~10 GB) |\n| **Safari / iOS** | **~1 GB** before prompting; expandable but user-gated |\n\n**Multi-GB reception is a desktop-Chromium story.** The app MUST query\n`navigator.storage.estimate()` up front and refuse clearly (§13.1) rather than failing at\nhour 9. With compression on, staging needs the compressed size *plus* the output.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance scenarios\n\nNamed, independently verifiable, with explicit pass **and fail** criteria. \"Fail\" means\nstop and reconsider the design, not retry.\n\n| # | Scenario | Setup | Action | Pass | Fail |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **A1** | Small file, ideal conditions | Laptop (1080p, 50% brightness min) → Pixel-class phone, 30 cm, office lighting (~300 lux), tripod | Send a 1 MB binary file (random bytes, incompressible) | Byte-identical output; ≥ 20 KB/s sustained; completes in ≤ 60 s | < 10 KB/s, or any byte differs |\n| **A1-lite** | Byte-exactness on two real devices | Two real devices (any configuration) | Send any file | Byte-identical output | Any byte differs |\n| **A2** | Handheld, realistic | As A1 but handheld, receiver held **portrait** (the default, unassisted grip — §6.3.2) | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≥ 10 KB/s | Does not complete in 5 min |\n| **A3** | Phone → phone | Two phones, 15 cm, handheld | Send 100 KB | Byte-identical; completes in ≤ 5 min | Does not complete — triggers §18 R4 |\n| **A4** | Lossy channel | A1 setup; camera deliberately occluded **5%** of the time in 2-second bursts (e.g., 2 seconds every 40 seconds) | Send 1 MB | Byte-identical; ≤ 1.3× the A1 frame count; completes in ≤ 90 s | Byte-incorrect OR > 2.0× A1 frame count OR does not complete in 3 min |\n| **A5** | Large file, memory flat | Desktop Chromium, synthetic 4 GB stream, headless block layer | Full encode→decode at the block layer | Byte-identical; peak heap ≤ 1 MB (I6a); no growth trend across 21,845 blocks | Any monotonic memory growth |\n| **A6** | Resume | A1 setup, 10 MB file | Reload the receiver tab at ~50% | Offers resume; completes; byte-identical | Restarts from zero, or completes with wrong bytes |\n| **A7** | Repair | A1 setup, 10 MB file, 5 blocks deliberately dropped | Enter the repair code on the sender | Only the missing blocks retransmit; completes in < 60 s | Full pass required |\n| **A8** | Offline | Both devices in airplane mode, app previously loaded | Full A1 transfer | Completes normally | Any network request attempted (asserted by CI, §14.4) |\n| **A9** | Wrong stream | Two senders visible in frame | Receiver points at both | Locks one `streamId`, ignores the other, says so | Mixes packets from both |\n| **A10** | Hostile beacon | Crafted beacon declaring `originalSize` = 281 TB | Receiver parses it | Refuses with `E-META-BOUNDS`; no allocation attempted | Allocates or crashes |\n\n**Adoption metrics are deliberately absent.** With no backend and no telemetry there is no\nway to measure them, and the ledger consciously cut the voluntary-benchmark idea. This is a\nstated limitation, not an oversight — see §18 R8.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Edge case catalog\n\n| # | Case | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| E1 | **Zero-byte file** | Reject at selection with `E-ZERO-BYTE-FILE`. `K = 0` is undefined. |\n| E2 | **File smaller than one fragment** (< 256 B) | Pad to one fragment; `K = 1`; the fountain code degenerates to repetition, which is correct. Research specifies a `K < 8` guard — adopt it: below 8 fragments, send plain repetition, no LT. **Repetition is derived per-block** (not signalled): both encoder and decoder derive `repetition = (k < MIN_LT_K)` from the block's K using the shared per-block derivation E3a already mandates. A session-wide flag would force repetition on all 21,845 blocks or none; per-block derivation allows the last block (K=1-7) to use repetition while all other blocks (K=768) use LT. |\n| E3a | **The last block is short** — its K is `ceil(lastLen / L)`, not 768. Both sides derive K per block, and D7's PRNG is seeded with it. A mismatch produces wrong index sets, so the block never decodes and nothing says why. | Derive per-block K from `(blockIndex, blockSize, payloadLen)` in **one shared function** used by both encoder and decoder; conformance vector covers the last block explicitly. The beacon's `payloadLen` field (§7.2) is critical — without it, the receiver cannot compute the last block's actual length (`lastLen = payloadLen − (blockCount − 1) × blockSize`), leading to PRNG index mismatch and silent decode failure. |\n| E3b | **`blockCount == 1`** | Normal path; no special case, but tested explicitly since off-by-one in block iteration is likely. |\n| E4 | **Incompressible input where deflate expands it** | D8 samples first; if the sample ratio > 0.92, skip compression. If compression still expands, discard the staging file and send raw. Emit `E-INCOMPRESSIBLE-EXPANDS` as a warning. |\n| E5 | **Source file changes mid-transfer** | A 10-hour read of a live `File` handle is the *normal* case. Re-check `file.size` and `lastModified` before each block read; on mismatch abort with `E-SOURCE-CHANGED`. Emitting blocks from two versions would produce a file that passes per-block hashes and fails the whole-file hash after hours. |\n| E6 | **Duplicate packet arrives** | GE reduces it to a zero row; contributes nothing, costs one reduction. No special handling. |\n| E7 | **Two senders in frame** | `streamId` lock (A9); packets from the unlocked stream are discarded and surfaced as `E-FOREIGN-STREAM`. |\n| E8 | **Tab backgrounded on the sender** | `rAF` stops in a background tab, so a 10-hour transfer silently halts. Wake Lock does **not** cover this. Detect via `visibilitychange` and warn loudly; the transfer is paused, not failed. |\n| E9 | **Camera permission revoked mid-run** | Pause, preserve the bitmap, prompt for re-grant. Never discard collected blocks. |\n| E10 | **OPFS quota exhausted mid-transfer** | Stop, keep completed blocks, export a partial file plus a manifest of what is missing. Never silently truncate. **The kept partial artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle** — warn the user before keeping it, provide a delete control, and reap on startup. |\n| E11 | **Abandoned staging file** | Sender-side staging keyed by `streamId`; on startup, reap staging files with no active session. Also a privacy requirement (§12, T4a). |\n| E12 | **Block hash verification fails** | After manifest arrives, block hash verification fails. Clear the verified bitmap bit, re-collect the block. Emit `E-BLOCK-HASH`. Block may already be written to OPFS but is never surfaced until verified (I9). This is the CRC-8 false-accept path (§7.1) and MUST be implemented — at GB scale a silent re-do costs hours. |\n| E13 | **Whole-file hash fails after all blocks pass** | Indicates E5 or a block-hash collision. Report `E-FILE-HASH`; keep the output and label it unverified rather than deleting hours of work. |\n| E14 | **Filename with path separators or control bytes** | Sanitise on export (§12, T2). Never write an attacker-chosen path. |\n| E15 | **Decompression fails at the end** | All blocks verified (per-block hashes passed) but the gzip stream is invalid → `E-DECOMPRESS`. Keep the compressed artefact so nothing is lost, but note that **the whole-file hash cannot be evaluated** — it requires successful decompression to compute. The kept artefact follows T4b's deletion lifecycle: warn the user before keeping it (explicitly noting it is **unverified**), provide a delete control, and reap on startup. The compressed artefact is received data that passed per-block verification but failed the final format conversion (decompression); it cannot be surfaced to the user as the original file. |\n| E16 | **Worker crash mid-block** | Restart the worker, discard the active block only, keep the bitmap. Emit `E-WORKER-CRASH`. |\n| E17a | **Sender-side thermal throttling** | Observed: the bench laptop decayed 6.7 → 2.4 fps over two minutes. Locally observable, so D18b's local step-down applies. **Receiver-side detection:** Camera fps drops >30% while decode latency stays within +30%. See `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md` for discrimination logic. The receiver MUST NOT duty-cycle in response to sender-side throttling — doing so would multiply transfer time without addressing the root cause. |\n| E17b | **Receiver-side thermal throttling** | Observed at **70 °C / throttling threshold within 20–30 minutes**. D18a's rule bites: fps decline is a *receiver* observation, the ladder is a *sender* control, and there is no back-channel — so \"step the ladder down\" is **structurally impossible** here. Mitigate locally instead: **duty-cycle (D27)** is the primary lever; drop decode resolution is often NOT viable because S3 showed 1080p was already at 2.25 camera px/module (below the 4 px/module cliff), and 720p measured 100% erasure. Resolution reduction MUST maintain ≥ 4 camera px/module floor. **Detection:** Decode latency increases >50% while camera fps stays within -20%. See `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md` for discrimination logic against sender-side throttling. |\n| E18 | **Resume offered for a file the user no longer has** (sender side) | `streamId` mismatch on re-selection → offer a fresh transfer with `E-RESUME-MISMATCH`, do not silently restart. |\n\n---\n\n## 11. Check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1059\t| `E-REPAIR-CODE` | Repair code checksum failed | \"That repair code doesn't look right — check it and try again.\" | user re-enters |\n1060\t| `E-FILE-HASH` | Whole-file hash failed (E13) | \"The file is complete but failed its final check — saved as unverified.\" | keep output, warn |\n1061\t| `E-WASM-LOAD` | Decoder failed to load | \"The scanner failed to start. Reload the page.\" | user reloads |\n1062\t\n1063\t**Status codes** (informational, not errors):\n1064\t\n1065\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing |\n1066\t|---|---|---|\n1067\t| `E-VERIFYING` | Verifying blocks against manifest (§7.6) | \"Verifying received chunks against manifest...\" |\n1068\t\n1069\t**Local / resource:**\n1070\t\n1071\t| Code | Meaning | User-facing | Recovery |\n1072\t|---|---|---|---|\n1073\t| `E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT` | Not enough storage (§13.1) | \"Not enough free space: this needs X, you have Y.\" | user frees space |\n1074\t| `E-QUOTA-EXHAUSTED` | Ran out mid-transfer (E10) | \"Out of space. Saved what arrived — X of Y chunks.\" | partial export |\n1075\t| `E-SOURCE-CHANGED` | Source mutated (E5) | \"The file changed while sending. Start again to avoid a corrupt copy.\" | restart required |\n1076\t| `E-BACKGROUNDED` | Sender tab backgrounded (E8) | \"Sending paused — keep this tab visible.\" | auto-resume on focus |\n1077\t| `E-CAMERA-LOST` | Permission revoked (E9) | \"Camera access ended. Your progress is saved.\" | re-grant, resume |\n1078\t| `E-WAKELOCK-LOST` | Screen may sleep | \"The screen may turn off. Adjust your sleep settings.\" | user acts |\n1079\t| `E-DECOMPRESS` | Decompression failed (E15) | \"Everything arrived but couldn't be unpacked. The raw data was kept.\" | keep artefact |\n1080\t\n1081\t---\n1082\t\n1083\t## 12. Threat model\n1084\t\n1085\tThe README claims \"provably no exfiltration\" and \"auditable once and trusted thereafter\".\n1086\tThat claim needs backing. In scope for v1:\n1087\t\n1088\t| # | Threat | Stance | Test |\n1089\t|---|---|---|---|\n1090\t| **T1** | **Crafted optical stream — resource exhaustion.** Beacon-declared `originalSize` and `payloadLen` (281 TB each), `blockCount` (16.7 M) and `L` are attacker-controlled and size allocations. | **Mitigated.** Bounds-check every beacon field before use: `L` ∈ [1, 4096], `K` ≤ locally benchmarked max (D26), `blockCount` ≤ 16.7 M, `originalSize` ≤ available quota, `payloadLen` ≤ available quota. Reject with `E-META-BOUNDS`. Never allocate from a declared size. | A10 + fuzz beacon fields |\n1091\t| **T2** | **Path traversal / hostile filename.** `filename` is attacker-supplied and reaches a save dialog. | **Mitigated.** Strip path separators, control bytes and leading dots; cap length; never pass through unsanitised. | unit: filenames with `../`, NUL, control bytes |\n1092\t| **T3** | **Decompression bomb.** The receiver decompresses attacker-supplied data. | **Mitigated.** Enforce a max expansion ratio (100:1) and an absolute cap = declared `originalSize`; abort with `E-DECOMPRESS` on overrun. | unit: 1 GB-expanding zip bomb → `E-DECOMPRESS` |\n1093\t| **T4a** | **Sender-side plaintext residue.** D8 writes a *decompressed-equivalent* copy of the user's file to OPFS as staging. For the flagship use case (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) this is real exposure. | **Mitigated.** Wipe staging on completion, on cancel, and on startup-reap (E11). Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest and the OS/browser may retain it. | integration: assert sender OPFS empty after complete/cancel/reap |\n1094\t| **T4b** | **Receiver-side plaintext residue.** The receiver stages the complete decoded file in OPFS. The output **is** the deliverable — it cannot be deleted immediately. For sensitive files (SSH keys, PSBTs, TOTP seeds) indefinite storage is exposure. | **Mitigated.** Implement a deletion lifecycle: (1) delete after successful `share()`/`save()`; (2) reap orphaned outputs on startup; (3) warn before keeping partial artefacts (E10, E15); (4) provide a user-visible delete control. Document that OPFS is not encrypted at rest. | integration: assert receiver OPFS empty after successful save; reap deletes orphans; UI has delete control; warning shown for partial artefacts |\n1095\t| **T5** | **Supply chain.** The security claim depends on the bundle being what was audited. | **Partially mitigated.** `bf-13h` covers the output half (version footer + published hash). The input half — pinned dependency versions, WASM integrity, no post-install scripts — is a Phase 0 requirement (§14.5). | G3: lockfile diff + SRI check in CI |\n1096\t| **T6** | **Shoulder-surfing / filming.** The optical channel is uniquely exposed: anyone with a camera in the room captures the same stream. | **Accepted for v1, consciously.** concept.md scopes encryption as a non-goal; §19 Q10 keeps it live. The app MUST NOT claim confidentiality it does not provide — the UI should say the transmission is visible to anyone who can see the screen. | none — accepted, not mitigated |\n1097\t| **T7** | **No telemetry, by construction.** | **Committed.** The app makes **zero** network requests after load. Enforced by CI (§14.4) and by A8. This is a stronger and more checkable claim than a privacy policy. | §14.4 network assertion + A8 |\n1098\t\n1099\t**Out of scope for v1, stated:** authenticating the *sender* (no PKI, no trust anchor); a\n1100\tmalicious *receiver* (it only gets what it is shown); side-channels other than the optical\n1101\tone; physical device compromise.\n1102\t\n1103\t---\n1104\t\n1105\t## 13. Performance budgets and benchmark contract\n1106\t\n1107\t### 13.1 Budgets — committed, not forecast\n1108\t\n1109\t§15's table is *expectation*. These are the numbers the build is held to.\n1110\t\n1111\t**Throughput basis.** All throughput budgets are **user-visible file bytes per second** after:\n1112\t- Fountain coding overhead (+12% p99 at K=768 with D25's cap)\n1113\t- Erasure loss (20–30% assumed band per D18c)\n1114\t- Dwell overhead (60% standing overhead per §8.1)\n1115\t\n1116\tThe gross wire rate at the R2 nominal rung (v16-L, 2 packets/tile, 15 tiles, 15 fps) is\n1117\t**112.5 KB/s payload** (7.5 KB/frame × 15 fps). After fountain (+12%) and 30% erasure,\n1118\tnet goodput is **~70 KB/s** — well above the 20 KB/s budget.\n1119\t\n1120\t| Budget | Value | Gate |\n1121\t|---|---|---|\n1122\t| **Bundle size (uncompressed)** | **≤ 200 kB** — JavaScript bundle delivered to browser | G3, Phase 0 |\n1123\t| **Bundle size (gzip)** | **≤ 65 kB** — Gzip-compressed JavaScript bundle | G3, Phase 0 |\n1124\t| Throughput, A1 reference setup | **≥ 20 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3 |\n1125\t| Throughput, A3 phone→phone | **≥ 3 KB/s** sustained | Phase 3; miss triggers §18 R4 |\n1126\t| Block-layer working set | **≤ 1 MB**, any file size (I6a) | Phase 1 |\n1127\t| Whole-receiver peak | **≤ 64 MB**, ≤ 4 in-flight `VideoFrame`s (I6b) | Phase 3 |\n1128\t| GE sustained XOR need | **≤ 200 MB/s** at the fastest supported stage (modelled 114.6 MB/s, 1.74× margin) — **measured 3,260 MB/s desktop / ~815 MB/s est. phone; the budget was ~16× pessimistic.** R1 provisionally closed, pending an on-device run *while thermally throttled* | Phase 1 + G7 |\n1129\t| Per-camera-frame decode | **≤ 60 ms** p99 (leaves headroom at 15 fps) — **measured 67–69 ms p50 full-frame, 194 ms at 4K, 6.6 ms with a tight ROI. p50 already exceeds the p99 budget**; the fixes (worker pool §6.2, tight ROI §6.4) are unimplemented, so this is violated by the instrument, not yet by the design | Phase 3 |\n1130\t| Encode + render per frame | **≤ 20 ms** p99 — **measured ~150 ms** (6.7 fps against 12 requested) on a 2015 laptop with D4's pinned mask unimplemented | Phase 3 |\n1131\t| Time-to-first-packet after aim | **≤ 3 s** p50 | Phase 5 |\n1132\t| Reception overhead vs K | **≤ +5%** mean, **≤ +12%** p99 (measured: +2.97% / +4.2%) | Phase 1, `sim/` |\n1133\t| **Sustained operation duration** | **≥ 20 min** sustained throughput within **30% of initial rate** on target phone (Pixel 6-class) without active cooling. This is the **minimum viable duration** before R11's thermal throttling mitigation (duty-cycle reduction) must engage. The system is not required to avoid throttling indefinitely—only to (a) sustain long enough for practical use and (b) detect and surface throttling when it occurs (E17b, D27). | Phase 3; validated by T-long-run |\n1134\t| **Warn threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 30 min** → explicit confirm | Phase 4 |\n1135\t| **Refuse threshold** (D23) | estimated duration **> 48 h per-session** (with resume), or quota insufficient → refuse with an override. At 70 KB/s goodput, 48 h ≈ 12 GB, covering the §1.1 headline case (10 GB at 27.5 h) with margin | Phase 4 |\n1136\t\n1137\t### 13.2 Benchmark denominator — the contract\n1138\t\n1139\tEvery throughput number in this repo MUST state all of these, or it is not a measurement:\n1140\t\n1141\t| Parameter | Reference value |\n1142\t|---|---|\n1143\t| **Unit** | **User-visible file bytes per second.** Not wire bytes. With compression these differ 3–10×. |\n1144\t| Sender | 1080p display, 50%+ brightness, DC-balanced frames |\n1145\t| Receiver | Mid-range Android (Pixel-6-class), rear camera |\n1146\t| Distance | 30 cm (laptop→phone), 15 cm (phone→phone) |\n1147\t| Mounting | Tripod for budget figures; handheld reported separately, never mixed |\n1148\t| Lighting | ~300 lux, no direct glare |\n1149\t| File | 1 MB of random bytes (incompressible) unless stated |\n1150\t| Duration | ≥ 60 s sustained; startup excluded |\n1151\t| Trials | ≥ 5; report median and p99, never the best run |\n1152\t\n1153\t**§15's comparison table mixes measurement regimes** — PixNet's 12 Mb/s used a 30\" LCD and\n1154\ta 24 MP DSLR. Such figures MUST be labelled with their regime and never compared directly\n1155\tto handheld numbers.\n1156\t\n1157\t---\n1158\t\n1159\t## 14. Testing strategy and quality gates\n1160\t\n1161\t### 14.1 Tiers\n1162\t\n1163\t| Tier | What | Runs |\n1164\t|---|---|---|\n1165\t| **T-unit** | Codec internals, header parse, CRC, bitmap, repair-code round-trip | Every commit |\n1166\t| **T-property** | Random files × random loss patterns → byte-exact; overhead within simulation bounds | Every commit |\n1167\t| **T-stub-camera** | `getUserMedia` stubbed with `canvas.captureStream(0)` + `requestFrame()`. No flags, frame-exact, deterministic | Every commit |\n1168\t| **T-degradation** | Synthetic blur / rotation / keystone / glare / rolling-shutter tearing applied to rendered frames. **Assert decode *rates*, not booleans** | Nightly |\n1169\t| **T-real-capture** | Frames → Y4M → Chromium fake camera. Proven in research (byte-exact, including late-join at 700 ms) | Nightly |\n1170\t| **T-scale** | Synthetic 4 GB stream at the block layer; assert flat memory across 21,845 blocks | Nightly |\n1171\t| **T-long-run** | **20–30 minute sustained run** on real devices to validate thermal behavior (R11), duty-cycle economics (D27), and sustained throughput. Tracks fps decline, decode rate, and effective goodput over time. **This is the ONLY tier that can measure R11 and D27** — the 60 s floor in §13.2 structurally excludes thermal phenomena. | Weekly (or per thermal-related change) |\n1172\t| **T-physical-rig** | Two real devices, fixed mounting, the §13.2 denominator. **This is the acceptance gate for §13.1 throughput** — nothing else can measure it | Per release |\n1173\t| **T-manual-iOS** | Full pass on a real iPhone. **Not CI-testable at any price** — WebKit cannot fake a camera, the Simulator has none | Per release |\n1174\t\n1175\t> **Trap, already paid for:** `--use-fake-device-for-media-capture` **does not exist**. It\n1176\t> is `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream`, and the file flag requires it.\n1177\t\n1178\t### 14.2 Binary-safety testing\n1179\t\n1180\t**MUST use real compressed payloads at several lengths — never ASCII.** Corruption in the\n1181\trejected libraries was both *content*- and *length*-dependent: the same generator\n1182\tround-tripped at 600 bytes and corrupted at 256. An ASCII suite marks every library safe,\n1183\tincluding the broken ones. The nastiest case, `@zxing/library.getText()`, returns the\n1184\t**correct length** while collapsing bytes ≥ 0x80 to U+FFFD — a length assertion passes and\n1185\tthe file is silently ruined. Assert on bytes, at multiple lengths, over 0x00–0xFF.\n1186\t\n1187\t### 14.3 Conformance vectors\n1188\t\n1189\tShip as fixtures, because they are what a third-party implementation would need:\n1190\t\n1191\t- `(streamId, blockIndex, seq) → index set` — bit-exact, pinning the PRNG (I3)\n1192\t- Header encode/decode round-trip at every field boundary\n1193\t- Beacon encode/decode including absent optional fields\n1194\t- Repair-code round-trip, including a deliberately mistyped code\n1195\t- A **two-realm test**: the same built app in two contexts, one sending, one receiving —\n1196\t  the only test that actually verifies the \"both roles, one page\" constraint\n1197\t\n1198\t### 14.4 The no-network assertion\n1199\t\n1200\tCI MUST fail the build if the running app issues **any** network request after load —\n1201\tincluding the lazy WASM fetch described in §6.5, which is the most likely violation and\n1202\tdoes not occur until the first decode, so **the assertion must exercise a decode**\n1203\t(intercept `fetch`/`XHR`/`WebSocket`/`EventSource`/`Image`; fail on any call). This is the\n1204\texecutable form of T7 and of concept.md constraint 1.\n1205\t\n1206\t### 14.5 Quality gates\n1207\t\n1208\t| Gate | Requirement |\n1209\t|---|---|\n1210\t| **G1** | Typecheck, lint, unit, property, stub-camera all green |\n1211\t| **G2** | No network requests (§14.4) |\n1212\t| **G3** | Bundle-size budget not exceeded; dependencies pinned to exact versions, no post-install scripts (T5) |\n1213\t| **G4** | Simulation assertions for D5/D6/D25 pass (I2), **at the adopted K** |\n1214\t| **G5** | Memory budget (I6a) holds on T-scale. **Runs nightly**, so it gates the nightly build, not each commit — see the cadence note below |\n1215\t| **G6** | Throughput budgets (§13.1) hold on T-physical-rig — release only |\n1216\t| **G7** | `python3 docs/research/sim/ge_cost_model.py --check` passes — **the plan's §3.1/§4 numbers match what the model computes**. This exists because every critical defect found in review was a bookkeeping failure attached to correct reasoning; making the numbers executable removes the class |\n1217\t\n1218\t**All-gates-same-commit:** G1–G4 and **G7** MUST pass on the *same* commit — these are\n1219\tfast. G5 is nightly and gates the nightly build; G6 is release-only. A green build\n1220\tassembled from different commits is not a green build.\n1221\t\n1222\t### 14.6 Definition of done\n1223\t\n1224\tA phase is done when: its exit criteria (§17) are met; G1–G4 and G7 are green on one commit\n1225\t(G5 is nightly and gates the nightly build per §14.5); every new failure mode has a test;\n1226\tevery new error code has a user-facing string; and the plan is updated if any decision changed.\n1227\t\n1228\t**Stop-ship criteria** — do not release if: any A-scenario fails; I1–I10 are unenforced;\n1229\ta data-loss path exists without a test; or the version footer is absent (a user cannot\n1230\ttell what they are running).\n1231\t\n1232\t---\n1233\t\n1234\t## 15. Throughput expectations\n1235\t\n1236\t*Forecasts from research. The committed numbers are §13.1.*\n1237\t\n1238\t| Stage | Approach | Expected | Regime |\n1239\t|---|---|---|---|\n1240\t| — | Single QR (what most projects do) | 1–9 KB/s | handheld, matches TXQR |\n1241\t| **1** | **Tiled monochrome QR** | **20–45 KB/s** | tripod, laptop→phone |\n1242\t| **2** | **+ RGB channel tripling** | **35–90 KB/s** | tripod |\n1243\t| **3** | **libcimbar-derived codec** | **~106 KB/s** | libcimbar's published figure, monitor→phone. **Its advantage is frame rate, not density** — see below |\n1244\t| — | Phone-to-phone research SOTA | ~40 KB/s | lab, mounted |\n1245\t| — | All-time lab record (PixNet) | 12 Mb/s | **30\" LCD + 24 MP DSLR — not comparable** |\n1246\t\n1247\t**Stage 3's rationale — corrected.** An earlier revision of this section claimed *\"QR is denser\n1248\tper pixel than libcimbar\"* (0.0794 vs 0.0741 bits/screen px²) and used it to push symbology to\n1249\tlast place. **That comparison was invalid, and in exactly the way AP1 warns about:** the 0.0794\n1250\tfigure is QR v16-L at **3** screen px/module, below this plan's own ≥ 4 camera px/module decode\n1251\tfloor. Compared at a size that actually decodes:\n1252\t\n1253\t| Scheme | Bits per screen px² (at its decode floor) |\n1254\t|---|---|\n1255\t| QR v16-L @ **4** px/module | **0.0447** |\n1256\t| libcimbar, 6 bits over 9×9 px | **0.0741** |\n1257\t| *(QR v16-L @ 3 px/module — below the floor, not comparable)* | *0.0794* |\n1258\t\n1259\t**libcimbar is ~1.66× denser per pixel at a decodable cell size**, and it also sustains ~11\n1260\tdecoded frames/s where the rig managed 2–4. So its advantage is **both** density and frame\n1261\trate, and Stage 3 is *more* attractive than the corrected-away version suggested — not less.\n1262\t\n1263\tWhat survives from that reasoning: **decode CPU per bit is the metric that matters**, and the\n1264\tcheap decode-side wins (worker pool, tight ROI, capture resolution, D27) come first because\n1265\tthey are cheap, not because symbology is worthless. **R7 (MPL-2.0 licensing) and §19 Q1 are\n1266\ttherefore NOT de-urgentised** — they gate Phase 7 and Phase 7 is worth reaching.\n1267\t\n1268\t**The dominant risk is geometry, not software.** Cell size is set by how many *camera\n1269\tpixels* the sender's screen occupies:\n1270\t\n1271\t- Laptop → phone at 30 cm: ~1325 px across ≈ 165-cell grid\n1272\t- **Phone → phone: ~327 px across ≈ 54 cells — one ninth the capacity**\n1273\t\n1274\tPhone→phone is also bounded by **minimum focus distance**: filling the frame needs ~6.6 cm,\n1275\tinside the ~10 cm focus limit, so the symbol spans only 50–60% of frame.\n1276\t\n1277\t---\n1278\t\n1279\t## 16. Platform and operations\n1280\t\n1281\t### 16.1 iOS — the binding platform\n1282\t\n1283\t- **No Web Share Target, ever.** \"Share → screenferry\" cannot exist on iOS.\n1284\t- **No File System Access API.** Output must be `navigator.share({files})`, gated on\n1285\t  `canShare`, fired from a **real touch handler**. iOS ignores programmatic blob-anchor\n1286\t  clicks. **Multi-GB export via `share()` is untested and likely to fail** (§19 Q9).\n1287\t- Inbound: `<input type=file>` with **no `accept`** — forces Files, avoids silent\n1288\t  HEIC→JPEG transcoding.\n1289\t- **Service-worker cache deleted after 7 days** unless installed to Home Screen (D13).\n1290\t- **iPhone cannot go fullscreen** (iPad only); standalone display mode substitutes.\n1291\t- **Wake Lock only in Home Screen web apps, iOS 18.4+.** A `pushState` path change kills a\n1292\t  live stream — routing MUST NOT touch the path during capture.\n1293\t- **No `BarcodeDetector`** — and it is structurally unusable everywhere anyway: the spec's\n1294\t  `DetectedBarcode` has **no byte member**.\n1295\t- **No image-capture extensions** — no `exposureCompensation`, so D14's fix does not apply.\n1296\t- **~1 GB storage quota** (§8.4).\n1297\t\n1298\t### 16.2 Deployment\n1299\t\n1300\tStatic bundle to a static host (Cloudflare Pages or equivalent), built in CI on iad-ci.\n1301\tNo backend, no database, no migration. Rollback is redeploying the previous bundle —\n1302\t**but see §16.3, which is what makes rollback non-trivial.**\n1303\t\n1304\t### 16.3 Version skew — the one operations item that genuinely applies\n1305\t\n1306\tTwo devices each hold an independently-cached copy of the app. A static host that updates,\n1307\ta service worker that caches for offline use, and iOS's 7-day eviction mean **device A can\n1308\tbe running a month-old build while device B loads today's**.\n1309\t\n1310\t| Rule | |\n1311\t|---|---|\n1312\t| **Version fields** | The header's 4-bit nibble is a *fast reject* only; the beacon's 1-byte `wireVersion` is authoritative. The nibble is `wireVersion & 0x0F`, so it **wraps after 16 bumps** — a receiver MUST NOT treat a nibble match as compatibility, only as \"worth parsing the beacon\". |\n1313\t| **Wire compatibility** | The beacon's `wireVersion` gates the wire format. A receiver seeing an unknown version MUST report `E-VERSION` with both versions shown and refuse — **never attempt a partial parse**. |\n1314\t| **What is breaking** | Any change to header layout, beacon layout, PRNG, degree distribution, or fragment semantics. Bump `magic_ver`. |\n1315\t| **What is not** | UI, coaching, profile ladder tuning, dwell, new *optional* beacon fields appended at the end. |\n1316\t| **Stage coexistence** | Stage 1/2/3 modulations are distinguished by the beacon's `flags`, not by `magic_ver` — a Stage-1-only receiver MUST ignore colour tiles rather than fail. |\n1317\t| **Rollback consequence** | Rolling the sender back may strand receivers holding a newer cached build. So a wire-version bump is a **one-way door** and MUST be treated as such: ship it only when the previous version has been deployed long enough to be widely cached — **minimum 30 days**, since iOS evicts uninstalled caches at 7 days and D13-installed apps may lag far longer. |\n1318\t| **Update UX** | The service worker SHOULD prompt for update rather than swapping silently mid-transfer. Swapping during a 10-hour transfer would be fatal. |\n1319\t\n1320\t### 16.4 Health check\n1321\t\n1322\tOne pre-flight, run before the user commits, combining what is currently scattered across\n1323\tthree beads: storage estimate (`bf-4d6`), camera capability and measured fps (D14), wake\n1324\tlock availability, OPFS write test, and the calibration probe (D11). It refuses or warns\n1325\t**as one gate** with numeric thresholds (§13.1) rather than as three separate surprises.\n1326\t\n1327\t---\n1328\t\n1329\t## 17. Phases\n1330\t\n1331\tEach phase has **entry criteria** (what must be green before starting) and **exit\n1332\tcriteria** (testable). Phases 1–3 are the critical path; the parallel track can proceed\n1333\tindependently once Phase 0 lands.\n1334\t\n1335\t| Phase | Entry | Exit |\n1336\t|---|---|---|\n1337\t| **0 — Repo and harness** ⚠️ *partial* | — | Builds, deploys, version footer present, stub-camera tier runs, G1–G3 and **G7** green, **module layout (§6.5) and dependency pins committed**, and a throwaway end-to-end spike (one tiny file through a no-op modulation) proves the seams line up |\n1338\t| **0.5 — Spike** ⚠️ *partial* | Phase 0 exit | S1–S4 run and recorded in `docs/notes/spike-results.md`; §13.1's forecast rows replaced with measured figures or the relevant §18 risk triggered. **Gates Phase 1 because it sets K, L, dwell and the rung ladder.** See `spike/README.md` |\n1339\t| **1 — Core codec, headless** ⚠️ *built, gates unmet* | Phase 0.5 exit | 10 MB file survives 50% loss byte-exact; overhead within `sim/` bounds; synthetic 4 GB at flat ≤ 1 MB (A5 / I6a); GE keeps pace at K=768 measured on a real phone; G1–G5 green |\n1340\t| **2 — Single-QR optical loop — the walking skeleton** | Phase 1 exit | **A1-lite passes** (byte-exactness on two real devices, no throughput floor). **This is the first demonstrable end-to-end transfer**; Phase 0's spike is a seam check, not a product |\n1341\t| **3 — Tiling + fixed-weight ladder (D18a)** | Phase 2 exit | A1 ≥ 20 KB/s, A2, A3, A4 pass on T-physical-rig; G6 green |\n1342\t| **4 — Large-file machinery** | Phase 3 exit | A5, A6, A7, A10 pass; quota pre-flight refuses correctly; repair code round-trips |\n1343\t| **5 — The app + local ladder adaptation (D18b)** | Phase 4 exit | A8, A9 pass; every §11 error code has a user-facing string and is reachable; iOS manual pass; non-technical user completes a transfer unaided |\n1344\t| **6 — Calibration probe + colour** | Phase 5 exit | Probe reports device cutoffs; colour enabled only where it measurably wins; A1 improves or colour stays off |\n1345\t| **7 — Custom codec** | Phase 6 exit **and** the §19 Q1 licensing decision recorded | Stage 3 beats Stage 2 on T-physical-rig |\n1346\t\n1347\t### 17.1 Phase 0.5 — why a spike, and why here\n1348\t\n1349\tThe plan's parameters are currently modelled or borrowed from research on other\n1350\tpeople's hardware. The spike does not decide **whether** to build the codec — the\n1351\tfountain code, block layer and framing are needed whatever the channel does. Self-reinforcing loop: SoC slows → decode slower → camera fps falls → erasure rises → transfer lengthens → more heat | **Trigger:** Discriminate sender-side (camera fps drops >30%, decode latency within +30%) vs receiver-side (decode latency increases >50%, camera fps within -20%) throttling per `docs/notes/bf-3mnt-thermal-throttling-discrimination.md`. They are collected here because\n1452\teach was previously buried in the narrative of the section that fixed it, where an implementer\n1453\tstarting a later phase would never encounter it.\n1454\t\n1455\t| # | Anti-pattern | What it looked like | Guard |\n1456\t|---|---|---|---|\n1457\t| **AP1** | **A unit-free \"px/module\"** | Every optical run sat at 2.25 camera px/module while the config said \"4\". Presented as a symbology limit; was a sampling limit. | §2 defines screen px and camera px. Never write \"px/module\" unqualified. |\n1458\t| **AP2** | **The ROI ratchet** | A frame where only two tiles decoded shrank the crop to those two; every later frame then saw only that region and could never recover. Erasure 91%, goodput **worse than no cropping**, and it presents as an *optical* fault. | Wide margin (≥35%) **plus a forced full-frame rescan every N frames**. An ROI that can only shrink is a bug. |\n1459\t| **AP3** | **Sizing K from GE's memory term** | K = 16,384 gave a 32 MB matrix (fine) and needed 4.5 GB/s of XOR (23× over). | K is bound by *time*, not memory (§3.1). Faster wire rate makes decode **harder**. |\n1460\t| **AP4** | **Setting L from the nominal ladder rung** | L = 507 made the conservative rung carry **zero** packets, destroying the ladder's only guarantee. | L is set by the **smallest** rung (§3.1.1); `params.ts` throws at import if a rung cannot hold a whole packet. |\n1461\t| **AP5** | **Running the sender faster than D9 allows** | 2.8× over the half-camera-fps rule → 78% erasure. Looked like poor optics. | D9 is a constraint to satisfy, not a dial to maximise. |\n1462\t| **AP6** | **Narrowing the erasure band instead of raising dwell** | Contradicted the evidence base and cost throughput for no arithmetic reason. | Raise dwell; the band is an assumption about the channel (D18c), not a target. |\n1463\t| **AP7** | **Trusting `getSettings()` / requested capture** | Reports 30/60 fps while delivering 15; defaults to 1080 on the *short* edge. | Measure delivered fps and actual capture dimensions (D14, §6.4). |\n1464\t| **AP8** | **`--use-fake-device-for-media-capture`** | Does not exist. It is `--use-fake-device-for-media-**stream**`. | §14.1. |\n1465\t| **AP9** | **Never offering a torch button** | 3.6× fps gain makes it tempting; an LED on glossy glass destroys a region of the frame. | §6.4. |\n1466\t| **AP10** | **Writing a comment that asserts a file exists** | `prng.ts` claimed `test/fixtures/vectors.json` pinned the wire format. It did not exist. | Generate the artifact in the same commit as the claim (§14.3). |\n1467\t\n1468\t### 18.2 Proof obligations\n1469\t\n1470\tEach load-bearing assumption, what must be true, and what would invalidate it. Open questions\n1485\t\n1486\t1. **Licensing — decide before Phase 7, consciously.** libcimbar is **MPL-2.0**\n1487\t   (file-level copyleft); screenferry is MIT. Over a\n1494\t   10-hour transfer this matters far more than over 30 seconds. **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n1495\t5. **Should the sender ever stop?** It loops forever; at GB scale \"forever\" may be days.\n1496\t   **Resolve in Phase 5.**\n1497\t6. **Delta transfer vs fixed blocks** — see §20.2. **Resolve before Phase 4 implementation.**\n1498\t7. **Closed-loop negotiation — deferred on evidence.** Bidirectional links are precedented\n1499\t   (MAMBA: two phones, 11–28 kbps each way), but MAMBA's measured gain from closing the\n1500\t   loop is only **5–20%**, while changing the coding paradigm buys multiples. The PWA offline story is unaffected.\n1529\t\n1530\t### 20.1 Photosensitivity changes a rendering decision (`bf-6d3`)\n1531\t\n1532\tWCAG 2.3.1 caps general flashes at three per second **or** requires the flashing area to\n1533\tstay under the small-safe threshold. A full-bleed high-contrast animation at 12–15 fps for\n1534\thours is a genuine seizure risk.\n1535\t\n1536\t**The mitigation costs the core metric.** Bounding flash area reduces usable screen area →\n1537\tfewer cells → less throughput. The compliant design is therefore **a bounded coded region\n1538\tinside a static surround**, not full-bleed, and the area cost MUST be measured in Phase 3\n1539\trather than assumed. D10's DC balancing is part of this mitigation, not just an\n1540\tauto-exposure fix: constant mean luminance is far less provocative than alternating fields.\n1541\t\n1542\t### 20.2 Delta transfer tensions with the block design (`bf-280`)\n1543\t\n1544\t**A partially-received file *is* \"a file the receiver already has\"** — so\n1545\tresume-after-interruption and delta transfer are one mechanism at two granularities.\n1546\t\n1547\tBut general delta wants **content-defined chunking** (rolling hash, variable boundaries),\n1548\twhich contradicts I1 (L fixed) and D19 (fixed blocks, K derived). Two ways out:\n1549\t\n1550\t1. **Scope delta as a v2 mode with its own block scheme** — cleanest; the fixed-block path\n1551\t   stays untouched.\n1552\t2. **Keep fixed blocks and diff at block granularity** — no rolling hash, but only detects\n1553\t   changes aligned to 192 KB boundaries, so an insertion near the start re-sends\n1554\t   everything after it.\n1555\t\n1556\tOption 2 is dramatically cheaper and probably sufficient for the air-gapped-update case,\n1557\twhere changes are usually appends or whole-component replacements. **Start there.** The\n1558\tnear-term half — robust cross-session resume — has no such tension and ships first.\n1559\t\n1560\t---\n1561\t\n1562\t## 21.
